extracted.intended_audience: mariners, bridge owners/operators (Nassau County), local governments, small businesses potentially affected, and members of the public interested in commenting on the drawbridge operating schedule
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and procedural standards for a temporary interim Coast Guard rule modifying drawbridge operations and for public participation (submission and content of comments) on that rule. Covers statutory bases for bypassing normal notice-and-comment, regulatory analyses, small-entity considerations, environmental categorization, and how to submit/view comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good cause to issue rule without NPRM (5 U.S.C. 553(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 5 U.S.C. 553(b) an agency may issue a rule without prior notice and opportunity to comment when the agency for good cause finds that those procedures are 'impracticable, unnecessary, or contrary to the public interest.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Coast Guard found good cause because the bridge is operating under single leaf openings and cannot be brought back to normal operations until rehabilitation is complete, making it impracticable to provide a normal comment period before issuing the modification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good cause for shortened effective date (5 U.S.C. 553(d)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 5 U.S.C. 553(d)(3) an agency may make a rule effective in less than 30 days after publication if it finds good cause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Coast Guard finds delaying the effective date would be impracticable and contrary to the public interest because the bridge is incapable of normal operations and needs the modification in effect immediately to allow rehabilitation to proceed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significant regulatory action / Executive Order review (EO 12866 & 13563)
rubrics_metrics.description: Executive Orders 12866 and 13563 direct agencies to assess costs and benefits of regulatory alternatives and to select approaches that maximize net benefits; actions designated 'significant regulatory action' must be reviewed by OMB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This temporary interim rule was determined not to be a 'significant regulatory action' under EO 12866 (as amended). Accordingly, the rule was not reviewed by OMB. The determination was based on the ability for vessels to transit via single leaf operation and that vessels not requiring an opening may transit without impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory Flexibility Act (RFA) — small entity impact consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: The RFA (5 U.S.C. 601-612) requires agencies to consider potential impacts of regulations on small entities and, if appropriate, analyze alternatives; agencies may certify under 5 U.S.C. 605(b) if a rule would not have a significant economic impact on a substantial number of small entities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Coast Guard certified under 5 U.S.C. 605(b) that this rule would not have a significant economic impact on a substantial number of small entities. If an entity believes it qualifies as a small entity and that the rule would have significant economic impact, it should submit a comment explaining qualification and the degree of economic effect. The Coast Guard offers assistance and will not retaliate against small entities that question or complain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paperwork Reduction Act compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: The Paperwork Reduction Act (44 U.S.C. 3501-3520) governs new collections of information by federal agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This rule calls for no new collection of information under the Paperwork Reduction Act of 1995.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federalism and tribal implications analysis (EO 13132 & EO 13175)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules must be analyzed for federalism implications under EO 13132 and for tribal implications under EO 13175, i.e., whether they have substantial direct effects on States or Indian tribes or affect distribution of power.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Coast Guard analyzed this rule and determined it is consistent with federalism principles and has no tribal implications because it would not have substantial direct effects on States or Indian tribes or on the distribution of power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unfunded Mandates assessment (Unfunded Mandates Reform Act)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the Unfunded Mandates Reform Act agencies must assess effects of discretionary regulatory actions, particularly if they may result in expenditures of $100,000,000 or more in any one year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Coast Guard determined this rule will not result in expenditures meeting that threshold, though it discusses the Act's requirements in the preamble.

rubrics_metrics.name: NEPA / Environmental planning — categorical exclusion for drawbridge operation rules
rubrics_metrics.description: NEPA requires agencies to evaluate environmental effects of actions; DHS/Coast Guard implementing instructions identify categories of actions excluded from further NEPA review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Coast Guard determined this action is a category of actions that do not individually or cumulatively have a significant effect on the human environment and is categorically excluded under paragraph L49, of Chapter 3, Table 3-1 of the U.S. Coast Guard Environmental Planning Implementation Procedures. Neither a Record of Environmental Consideration nor a Memorandum for the Record are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to submit comments (format and content expectations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments should include the docket number for the rulemaking, indicate the specific section of the document to which each comment applies, and provide a reason for each suggestion or recommendation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Coast Guard encourages submission via the Federal Decision-Making Portal (regulations.gov). If unable to use regulations.gov, contact the person in FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT for alternate instructions. The agency will review all comments received but will only post comments that address the topic of the rule; it may choose not to post off-topic, inappropriate, or duplicate comments. Comments we post will include any personal information you provide. See DHS's eRulemaking System of Records (85 FR 14226) for more on privacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment logistics: docket access and deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Instructions for locating the docket and supporting materials and the deadline for receipt of comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To view documents, go to https://www.regulations.gov, type docket number USCG-2022-0891 in the search box, click 'Search', and select 'Supporting & Related Material' in the Document Type column. Comments and related material must reach the Coast Guard on or before September 25, 2023. Public comments will be placed in the online docket and viewable per regulations.gov FAQ guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment posting and anonymity policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether anonymous comments are accepted and how personal information is handled when posting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Coast Guard accepts anonymous comments. Comments posted to regulations.gov will include any personal information you have provided. The notice points to the DHS eRulemaking System of Records for privacy details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance for commenters to subscribe for updates
rubrics_metrics.description: Availability of subscription option for docket activity notifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Users can click the 'Dockets' tab for the rule and select the 'Subscribe' option to receive email alerts when comments are posted or when a final rule is published.
